question: Polarisation confirms that light is a transverse wave, but wave theory fails to explain the photoelectric effect completely. Explain why both statements are correct.

options.A: Polarisation demonstrates particle alignment, whereas the photoelectric effect is fully solved by classical continuous wave amplitude.
options.B: Polarisation supports the transverse wave nature of light, while the photoelectric effect cannot be explained by wave theory and requires the particle (photon) nature.
options.C: Both statements are correct because light behaves purely as a classical longitudinal wave in all mechanical interactions.
options.D: Polarisation requires a photon description, while the photoelectric effect demonstrates the continuous distribution of classical wavefront energy.
